transcript: Last night, I saw Vladimir at MTC, a new play which, contrary to what the title might suggest, is not really about Putin at all. It does take place in Russia at a time shortly after he was reelected in 2004 but he's not a character in this play. We're mostly following a few journalists who are reacting to and responding to the political sphere around them. As a bit of a thought piece, this play illustrates some different perspectives that tend to crop up during times of political extremism and mistrust. There's apathy and cynicism, and then there's resistance and interrogation. The subject matter here wasn't really my personal cup of tea, but this was a solid play with good writing and some interesting debate. I don't think this play really did much that I haven't seen before, but I think it could resonate with a good number of folks here in the US who find themselves burnt out by politics but still itching to decipher what their role is right now, socially and politically. With that, another playbill for my collection.
